messages:
elena: Heads-up — I opened a small PR that fixes an example mismatch in the API reference: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4321. The request example for POST /v1/ingest shows `user_id` (string) but the JS SDK snippet uses `user` and the schema lists `metadata` as required when it can actually be null. This is causing confusion for customers during migration.

matt: I saw that. Repro: legacy client sends `user: 'alice'` and server accepts but our conciser example shows `user_id: 'alice'`. Docs should match the canonical API (user_id). Also need to clarify `metadata` nullability. Current example has "metadata": null which reads weird in some SDK snippets.

samir: Do we have backwards-compat notes? If legacy SDKs send `user` we shouldn't break them unexpectedly. Maybe add a small migration note in the API ref that legacy clients can continue to send `user` until X date, but recommend `user_id` moving forward.

elena: Agree. Plan proposal in PR: (1) update example request/response to use `user_id` consistently, (2) show a small compatibility example for legacy clients (one-liner), (3) change schema description for `metadata` to "nullable object" and supply two example variants (null vs omitted), (4) update Python/Node SDK snippets to reflect the canonical fields.

matt: For the example variants we should show both concise and expanded forms. Example suggestions: 

```json
{
  "user_id": "alice",
  "content": "Hello",
  "metadata": {"source": "mobile"}
}
```

and

```json
{
  "user_id": "alice",
  "content": "Hello",
  "metadata": null
}
```

and mention "or omit `metadata` entirely for clients that don't have any." Keep the curl + SDK snippets in sync.

samir: Sounds good. Can we also add a short note in the migration guide (docs/migration/legacy-client.md) with the exact mapping? I can add the mapping table: `user -> user_id` and `ctx -> context` etc.

elena: I'll add the migration bullet and the examples in the PR. I'll also update the Python snippet to show `metadata=None` instead of `metadata={}` which is what caused the confusion with nullability earlier. I'll ping @matt for a quick review when ready.

matt: I'll review. Also can we add a tiny integration test in docs CI that renders the examples so we don't drift again? Just a smoke check that code blocks parse as JSON and fields present.

elena: Good idea — adding a single testcase under docs/test_examples/test_ingest_examples.py. Will include a link in PR description.

docs-bot: PR opened by elena: #4321 — "consistify ingest API examples + migration note". CI queued.

matt: :thumbsup: Thanks, Elena. Once CI passes and I review, we can merge and backport the migration note to the 1.x branch.

elena: I'll mark this as docs-owner and assign the backport if approved. Thanks all.
